title: A rink game on the rink core: a cartridge over thirdjam's match
summary: Hockey and its cousins are built on the rink core (engine/cores/rink: thirdjam's simulation and bots, compiled), never as a new simulation. The job starts from the base (the Foreman copies engine/templates/rink_game, hokej made skinnable) and changes data: the cartridge (rink, teams, speeds, contact, rules, zones, pickups, abilities, look, camera), the skin (title, team names, colours, words) and, only when a rule has no cartridge key, a rules sidecar. The house game engine/packs/hokej shows the whole route working.
applies_when: the game is played on a rink with sticks and a puck: hockey, pond hockey, shinny, bandy
the player skates one skater of a team; teammates and opponents are the core's bots
what the player asks for is a change of rink size, team sizes, rules, speeds, contact, zones, pickups, abilities, look or words
not_when: a ball that is kicked or bounces (soccer, football, basketball): that is not a cartridge of this core (a kick is a patch of the core's C++); use card.two_sides_ball or card.team_possession
a race or a vehicle: card.timed_drive

data_files.role: which cartridge the match plays (`cartridge`) and the bots' level (`difficulty`: rookie, pro, all_star)
the game: tj.cartridge/1 (game.rink, game.teams, game.skater, game.puck, game.shot, game.rules, game.look, game.camera); a mode is this file with only the keys it changes
the tl.rink.rules/1 sidecar: Third Life switches the cartridge schema cannot say; beside the cartridge it opens the rule-patched core

do: Start from the base: the plan's first package is of kind base (the Foreman copies the base; no builder) and the next package writes the game's cartridge, both in the first phase, so the first phase plays at once.

Change the cartridge, not the code: copy the nearest of thirdjam's twelve modes (ref/cores/rink/modes/MODES.md: Pond is 60 x 30, Marathon three a side on 140 x 70) and change only the keys the brief's CARTRIDGE lines name.
Put the game's words, title and team colours in the skin (data/skin.json), never in scripts.
Keep a mate who is not a back and an opponent chaser in every team list: the core's drill and the bots' shapes need them (MODES.md, the drill's mate).
Read the measured check (bash engine/tools/rink.sh check-cartridge <file>) beside the house game's: goals a match, passes a play minute, dead verbs.
dont: Never write a skating, puck, stick, contact, bot or camera script: the core has them, and they are why the house game feels like thirdjam.
Never preload anything under res://cores/ (lint N4): ctx.cores.open, view_script and part are the doors.
No key the schema does not know: unknown keys are errors, and the Foreman validates every cartridge edit before lint and smoke.

Three a side passes 0.2 to 0.8 times a play minute against 2.4 to 3.7 at five (MODES.md, team sizes): a small team needs the pass helped (pass_lead_frames, reception_m, carry_speed_mult) or it is a game of solo dashes.

bot.plays_by: a person's first match: PLAY NOW at ROOKIE, the same hand to the final whistle, through the keys
bot.wins_when: the match reaches its final whistle with the end card shown (the core decides the score)

acceptance: The pack opens the core with the game's cartridge (ctx.cores.open) and returns ctx.cores.state() from _pack_state, so the run's state hash holds the core's.
Every cartridge and rules file validates (foreman/src/cartridge.ts) and the measured check plays it: no dead verb, goals in a match.
The base's first match bot reaches the final whistle on the game's cartridge.
A person plays the first phase for five minutes and wants another go.

variants.change: copy the Pond mode (game.rink 60 x 30, corner 3, ice_friction 0.005, check_enabled false) and give game.teams three skaters each with a chaser and a support; help the pass (pass_lead_frames 20, stick.reception_m 3)
game.rules first_to 1 (the Sudden Death mode); keep five a side or the match is over in 23 s
game.pickups and game.abilities as the Arsenal mode (a boost_only zone at centre, speed and precision pickups, tricks on F)

camera: The core's camera bound to your skater (data: game.camera): behind and above, a short lag, the aim anchor; keep it, change only distance and height with the rink size.
juice: Words for the big moments go in big letters in the middle of the screen, apart from the score and the clock (a TLHudLayer text with an outline, or a center label of its own), and are gone when the moment ends: never added to the score line or the clock, never padded with blank lines into a tall slab; a word about the player says YOU ARE (never YOU IS), anyone else goes by the name the game shows; a word over a body is clamped whole inside the screen's safe area (5 % in from each edge), never cut by the edge.
The core's hit-stop and contact reads drive the figures (presentation only); a goal gets the base's horn, crowd and banner from the skin's words.
rivals: The opponents are thirdjam's bots at a level (data/match.json difficulty): easy by clumsiness, never by absence; name the team in the skin.
first_minute: PLAY NOW drops the puck at once; the base's HUD names what the two mouse buttons do with and without the puck.
stakes: One continuous match to the cartridge's score_to_win or its timer; the end card and a rematch on R.

estimate.source: the core plan's shape: the base (copied by the Foreman, no builder) plus a cartridge and a skin package; not yet measured on a real job

questions.reason: thirdjam's regular game is five a side; at three a side the human passes 0.2 to 0.8 times a play minute against 2.4 to 3.7 at five (MODES.md, team sizes)

questions.ask: How hard are the computer's skaters?
questions.reason: on thirdjam's set ladder the regular class wins 99 % of regular games at rookie, so its modes play pro (MODES.md, levels)
the base's cartridge plays first to 3 (game.rules.score_to_win 3)
